title: Badass Movie trope: A Character will 1. Light Cigarette 2. Puff once 3. Flick Cigarette away

commenti.body:
Well this is definitely a bit of an odd question, but I have an opinion. 

Smoking/cigarettes are traditionally seen as a sort of vice or indulgence, something a bit sinful, but permitted on a special occasion. That occasion happens to frequently be right before death. 

Prisoners were, irl, often offered a cigarette as part of their last meal/final request. It was done both as that indulgence and also as a way to calm the nerves before imminent death. For example, see the execution in *Valkyrie*. Iirc, a similar image is presented in *Paths of Glory*. 

In any case, the narrative lexicon of smoking a final cigarette has translated over to action films over the decades. Heroes will often light one up in the face of overwhelming odds or certain death. A suggestion of that “final indulgence” in a different, non-penal context. And because we don’t have time to sit and watch them smoke a whole cigarette down, we usually get the shorthand of someone lighting up, taking a few “soothing” drags, and then getting down to business. 

Smoking, especially “uncharacteristic smoking”, can always have other implications (for example, Mikael buying a pack of cigarettes, smoking one, and throwing the rest away, meant to imply an old habit that he is slowly backsliding into because of stress). But in specifically action-related context, I’d assume it’s visual shorthand for “odds ain’t lookin’ too good.”
